tagline: Around the Gunks, with one hairpin over the top.
intro: The byway rings the northern Shawangunk Mountains, said SHON-gum, for 88 miles through the Rondout and Wallkill valleys. Routes 44/55 climb over the ridge between Gardiner and Rondout Creek. Route 209 runs north through the farms of Kerhonkson and south through Wawarsing to Ellenville, where Route 52 climbs back into the mountains, and on the east side orchards line Route 208 from Wallkill to New Paltz, Apple Country in the byway's own words.
Up on the ridge are the Mohonk Preserve and Minnewaska State Park Preserve, with carriageways out to Lake Minnewaska and Lake Awosting. Down along Rondout Creek lie the old canal and cement towns.

moments.title: Rosendale Trestle
moments.text: The old rail trestle stands 150 feet over Rondout Creek, and after Conrail sold it for one dollar in 1986 its new owner tried to run it as a bungee jumping platform.

moments.title: Routes 44/55
moments.text: Past the Trapps Gateway the road takes a hairpin posted at five miles an hour and climbs a notch cut by cross-cutting faults to an overlook on the Wallkill Valley.

moments.title: Ellenville
moments.text: When the village leaders could not agree on a new name for the place, Ellen Snyder, sister of the tavern keeper's wife, persuaded them to name it after her.
